theater: 越南南部貢公、永隆與檳椖三區

battle.name: 三區革命
battle.theater: 越南南部貢公、永隆與檳椖三區
battle.brief: 三區革命於1944年1月在越南南部的貢公、永隆與檳椖爆發，越南獨立同盟武裝攻擊法國殖民行政與治安據點，形成三地連動的抗爭，是該組織早期對法殖民統治的大規模行動。英國海軍於1877年列裝的Torpedo boat，是高速近海作戰小艇，主要用魚雷攻擊水面艦船，並執行追擊與警戒。

kit.name: 魚雷艇
kit.history: Torpedo boat在英國海軍中屬小型高速水面作戰平台，配置於近岸部隊，以魚雷攻擊水面目標，並執行追擊、護航、巡邏與警戒任務。

countries: 「三區革命」爆發於一九四四年秋，戰區是廣東東部的海豐、陸豐、惠來三縣，亦即海陸惠地區。它不是兩支大軍沿單一戰線進行的會戰，而是原國民革命軍第十九路軍舊部，與中共領導的廣東人民抗日游擊隊共同發動的武裝起義，以及由此展開的一系列游擊戰鬥。日軍依靠城鎮、港口、廣汕鐵路和沿海公路維持控制，協日的地方武裝則據守部分鄉鎮與警察所；游擊總隊則以海陸、海惠公路兩側的山區為活動基地，在交通線與內陸之間反覆機動。國民黨第七戰區所屬部分地方武裝也曾奉命抗日，但由於前線退卻、指揮關係中斷和補給失靈，三方在同一區域內既可能短暫協同，也會發生摩擦。戰役由粵東沿海向內陸山地延伸，地理上始終是城鎮據點、公路護路、山區游擊與海上轉移互相交錯的戰鬥。
countriesEn: The Three Districts Revolution broke out in the autumn of 1944 in Haifeng, Lufeng, and Huilai in eastern Guangdong, an area known as the Hailu-Hui region. It was not a conventional meeting engagement fought by two large armies along a single front. It was an armed uprising jointly launched by former officers and soldiers of the National Revolutionary Army Nineteenth Route and the Communist-led Guangdong People's Anti-Japanese Guerrilla Force, followed by a series of guerrilla engagements. Japanese troops relied on the county towns, ports, the Guangzhou-Shantou Railway, and the coastal roads to maintain control, while collaborationist local armed units held some townships and police posts. The guerrilla corps used the hills on both sides of the Haifeng-Lufeng and Haifeng-Huilai roads as its operating base, repeatedly moving between the trunk transport routes and the interior. Some local troops under the Nationalist Seventh War Zone had also been ordered to fight the Japanese, but disrupted command relations and failed supply arrangements caused both temporary cooperation and armed friction in the same district. From the eastern Guangdong coast into the inland hills, this remained a struggle in which town garrisons, road escorts, mountain ambushes, and maritime movement constantly intersected.
people: 三區方面的核心領導是曾生、阮嘯仙與原十九路軍舊部吳文獻等軍事人員。曾生長期在海陸惠地區從事黨的組織工作和抗日武裝鬥爭，起義前已能聯絡當地游擊骨幹、東江交通線與內陸山區；在抗戰後期，他先統籌三區的武裝起義，統一部署襲擊、轉移和兵力使用，後來擔任廣東人民抗日遊擊總隊總隊長。阮嘯仙負責黨的領導、政治工作、幹部培訓以及與中共南方局的聯繫，後任總隊政治委員。他的作用不是只在作戰時宣讀命令，而是把原本分散於十九路軍舊部、共產黨游擊隊和地方武裝中的軍事單位納入同一套指揮與後勤關係。吳文獻是十九路軍在海陸惠一線的重要軍事聯絡人之一，在起義前後協助原十九路軍舊部與游擊隊接洽。參與者主要是各支隊官兵、偵察分隊、迫擊砲組、機槍組、救護與後勤人員，以及日軍守備隊和協日地方武裝；本文不把無法核實的普通士兵傷亡數字列為確定事實。
peopleEn: The central leaders on the Three Districts side were Zeng Sheng, Ruan Xiaoxian, and military personnel such as Wu Wenxian from the former Nineteenth Route. Zeng Sheng had long worked in the Hailu-Hui area on Party organization and armed resistance. Before the uprising he could already link local guerrilla cadres, the Dongjiang communications network, and the inland hill areas. In the latter part of the war he coordinated the armed uprising in the three districts, directing attacks, withdrawals, and the allocation of fighting strength; he later became commander of the Guangdong People's Anti-Japanese Guerrilla General Corps. Ruan Xiaoxian handled Party leadership, political work, cadre training, and liaison with the CCP Southern Bureau, after which he served as political commissar of the corps. His task was not merely to issue orders during battle, but to bring military units formerly dispersed among the old Nineteenth Route, Communist guerrillas, and local armed groups into a common command and logistics system. Wu Wenxian was an important military liaison for the Nineteenth Route in the Hailu-Hui area and assisted contacts between its former personnel and the guerrillas around the uprising. The participants were principally the officers and soldiers of the various columns, reconnaissance teams, mortar and machine-gun sections, medical and logistics personnel, together with Japanese garrisons and collaborationist armed units. This account does not present ordinary soldiers' casualty figures as settled facts when they cannot be verified.
kits: 三區游擊隊的武器並不統一，而是抗戰初期以漢陽八八式步槍及其後的七九式步槍為骨幹，另有少量中正式步槍；原十九路軍裝備中可見李-恩菲爾德Mk III長槍和ZB-26輕機槍。從日軍手中繳獲的六五式步槍則很快補入部隊，使同一分隊可能同時使用七九二毫米與六五毫米彈藥。輕武器包括馬牌一八九四年式駁殼手槍，遠射武器則有八二式迫擊砲和從日軍繳獲的二式五十毫米迫擊砲；機槍除ZB-26外，也包括日軍九七式重機槍與十一式輕機槍。手榴彈以九七式為主，並有中國軍隊使用的早期制式手榴彈。彈藥供應是最實際的限制：七九二乘五十七毫米、六五乘五十毫米、舊式七七毫米和英國七點六三毫米步槍彈不能彼此替代，五〇毫米與八二毫米迫擊砲彈亦須分開保管。遠距離轉移依靠馱騾、自行車和少量車輛，傷員使用帆布擔架，彈藥、糧食、藥品與通訊器材分散存放於沿途轉運點，反映出裝備來源不同補給週期也不同的實況。
kitsEn: The Three Districts guerrillas did not possess a standardized inventory. Their core infantry weapons were the Hanyang Type 88 rifle and the later Type 79-pattern rifle, with a smaller number of Chiang Kai-shek rifles. The old Nineteenth Route equipment included the Lee-Enfield Mk III long rifle and the ZB-26 light machine gun. Japanese Type 38 rifles captured from the enemy were quickly absorbed into the guerrillas, so one section could carry both 7.92-mm and 6.5-mm ammunition. Light weapons included the Mauser Model 1894 pistol, commonly known in China as the box pistol. Fire support came from the Chinese 82-mm mortar and captured Japanese Type 2 50-mm mortars, while machine-gun strength included the ZB-26, the Japanese Type 97 machine gun, and the Type 11 light machine gun. Type 97 hand grenades predominated, alongside earlier Chinese service grenades. Ammunition was the most practical constraint: 7.92-by-57-mm, 6.5-by-50-mm, older 7.7-mm, and British .303-inch rifle ammunition could not be substituted for one another, and 50-mm and 82-mm mortar rounds also had to be stored separately. Long-distance movement depended on pack mules, bicycles, and a limited number of vehicles. Stretchers carried the wounded, while ammunition, food, medicine, and communications equipment were dispersed among relay points along the routes, reflecting the fact that weapons from different sources also had different supply cycles.
tactics: 三區的行動以分散指揮和短距離集中兵力為基本方式。游擊總隊與十九路軍舊部先分別建立偵察關係，掌握日偽據點的駐防、巡邏、汽車班次和道路施工情況，再在同一夜晚向一個薄弱目標發動襲擊。步兵通常沿山間小路接近，先以手榴彈和步槍火力攻破門崗及哨位，奪取武器、通訊器材和糧食後即按預定路線撤回，不在城鎮或堡壘附近戀戰。公路伏擊多選在彎道、橋頭和狹窄路肩，機槍置於兩翼，迫擊砲從後方掩護；行動目的包括破壞橋梁、電報線、燃料庫與護路車隊，使日軍即使守住據點也要付出反覆護路兵力。遇到日偽集中掃蕩，游擊隊避免固定守點，通常分成數支小隊轉移，一座完成襲擊後立即換到另一條山路。海陸與海惠兩條公路因而成為反覆爭奪的骨架，而山區則提供游擊隊的宿營、整備與再攻擊條件。彈藥不足使他們更重視夜行、伏擊和短交火，很少進行正面衝鋒日軍主要城鎮的強攻。
tacticsEn: Operations in the Three Districts followed a pattern of decentralized command and temporary concentration of fighting strength. The guerrilla corps and the former Nineteenth Route personnel first established separate reconnaissance contacts, learning the garrison strengths, patrol schedules, vehicle convoys, and roadworks around Japanese and collaborationist posts. They then struck one weak target on the same night. Infantry approached along mountain tracks, used grenades and rifle fire against sentries and gate guards, seized weapons, communications equipment, and food, and then withdrew along prepared routes instead of remaining near a town or fortification. Road ambushes were normally placed at bends, bridgeheads, and narrow shoulders, with machine guns covering both flanks and mortars providing support from the rear. Targets included bridges, telegraph lines, fuel stores, and escorted convoys, forcing the Japanese to expend additional troops on road protection even where they retained their posts. When the enemy mounted concentrated sweeps, the guerrillas avoided fixed defenses and divided into several small columns that changed locations after each operation; once an attack was completed, the force moved to another mountain route. The Haifeng-Lufeng and Haifeng-Huilai roads therefore became the repeatedly contested framework of the campaign, while the hills supplied positions for rest, replenishment, and renewed attacks. ammunition shortages encouraged night movement, ambush, and brief engagements rather than frontal assaults on the principal Japanese-held towns.
data: 一九四四年四月十七日，豫湘桂會戰爆發，粵軍在西線與粵北的部署隨之動搖；到同年秋天，日軍加強粵東沿海與內陸交通線控制，第七戰區的地方指揮和補給也出現缺口。九月以後，曾生、阮嘯仙所掌握的游擊骨幹與吳文獻等十九路軍聯絡人完成接洽，依照中共南方局建立粵東抗日根據地和聯合抗日力量的部署，統籌海陸惠三區的行動。一九四四年十一月至十二月，首輪武裝起義和主要戰鬥展開：游擊隊攻擊日偽在公路沿線的薄弱哨所，截斷局部交通，並把繳獲武器迅速分散補充各支隊。同年十二月至一九四五年初，原有游擊大隊、地方武裝及十九路軍舊部完成整編，統一番號為廣東人民抗日遊擊總隊，曾生任總隊長、阮嘯仙任政治委員，按地區編成若干支隊及直屬分隊。一九四五年四月至五月，總隊配合全國戰場的反攻，在海陸、海惠公路和廣汕鐵路側翼發動連續襲擊。八月，總隊正式改編為東江縱隊；八月十五日日本宣布接受波茨坦宣言後，部分日軍孤立據點由游擊隊接收，九月三日投降生效時，戰鬥階段遂由殘餘日軍肅清轉入受降、繳械和部隊整編。
dataEn: The Operation Ichi-Go offensive began on 17 April 1944, and the disposition of Nationalist forces in the western and northern Guangdong fronts was shaken as a result. By autumn the Japanese had strengthened their hold over communications in eastern Guangdong, while local command and supply within the Seventh War Zone also broke down. After September, the guerrilla cadres under Zeng Sheng and Ruan Xiaoxian established contact with military liaison officers such as Wu Wenxian from the former Nineteenth Route. Following the Southern Bureau's plan to create an anti-Japanese base in eastern Guangdong and unite anti-Japanese armed forces, they coordinated operations across Haifeng, Lufeng, and Huilai. The first armed rising and principal engagements took place from November to December 1944: the guerrillas attacked weak Japanese and collaborationist posts along the roads, severed local communications, and rapidly distributed captured weapons among the columns. From December 1944 into early 1945, the former guerrilla units, local armed groups, and old Nineteenth Route personnel completed their reorganization under the Guangdong People's Anti-Japanese Guerrilla General Corps. Zeng Sheng became commander, Ruan Xiaoxian became political commissar, and the force was organized into regional columns and directly attached detachments. From April to May 1945, the corps supported the wider Chinese counteroffensive with repeated attacks along the flanks of the Haifeng-Lufeng and Haifeng-Huilai roads and the Guangzhou-Shantou Railway. In August the corps was formally reorganized as the Dongjiang Column. After Japan announced acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration on 15 August, guerrilla units took over a number of isolated Japanese positions. With the surrender taking effect on 3 September, the combat phase against residual Japanese forces gave way to the reception of surrenders, weapons collection, and unit reorganization.
cause: 三區革命由四項直接因素推動。第一，日軍在一九四四年下半年加強對粵東公路、鐵路、港口和城鎮的控制，護路與守點兵力增加，使游擊隊若不先建立山區基地，便難以保存實力。第二，豫湘桂會戰引發的西線退卻，削弱了廣東地方部隊的指揮與補給；第七戰區一些團隊雖仍具有抗日意願，卻因失聯、換防和軍械不足而各自行動，原十九路軍舊部也需要重新建立軍事聯繫。第三，中共南方局以建立抗日根據地、發展游擊力量和團結各派抗日武裝為部署，使曾生、阮嘯仙與地方黨組織能將原有游擊隊整合成跨縣的統一指揮系統。第四，三區內存在道路沿線據點與山區武裝並存的局面，日偽能集中兵力控制城鎮，游擊隊則可利用分散哨位、交通死角和縱深山地。雙方在控制能力上的差距，迫使游擊隊採取夜襲、伏擊、破壞和反覆轉移，而十九路軍舊部帶來的常備軍經驗、舊部關係與部分武器，又提供了編組和訓練上的補充。
causeEn: Four immediate factors drove the Three Districts Revolution. First, during the second half of 1944 the Japanese strengthened their control over roads, railways, ports, and towns in eastern Guangdong. The increase in troops assigned to road security and garrison defense meant that the guerrillas had to establish an inland base before they could preserve their strength. Second, the westward withdrawal associated with Operation Ichi-Go disrupted command and supply for local Guangdong forces. Some units under the Seventh War Zone still wished to resist Japan, but changes of position, interrupted communications, and shortages of weapons left them operating independently; the old Nineteenth Route personnel likewise needed to rebuild military contacts. Third, the CCP Southern Bureau directed the creation of an anti-Japanese base area, the expansion of guerrilla strength, and the unification of all anti-Japanese armed groups. This enabled Zeng Sheng, Ruan Xiaoxian, and the local Party organization to integrate existing guerrillas into a command structure spanning three counties. Fourth, Japanese and collaborationist forces could concentrate on the towns, while the guerrillas exploited dispersed posts, gaps in the transport network, and the depth of the interior hills. This disparity forced the guerrillas toward night attacks, ambushes, disruption, and repeated movement, while the old Nineteenth Route contributed regular-army experience, former service contacts, and part of the weapons needed for organization and training.
impact: 三區行動首先改變了日偽在粵東的兵力配置。游擊隊不斷襲擊護路車隊、燃料庫和孤立哨所，使日軍不能只依賴城內駐軍，而要從其他戰線抽調步兵、工兵與運輸單位維持道路安全；公路因此不再能像此前那樣由小型巡邏隊安全通行。其次，原十九路軍舊部與中共游擊隊之間形成了實際的聯合參謀、掩護撤退、分散寄存武器和統一後勤關係，總隊由若干互不隸屬的武裝逐步轉為以支隊為骨幹的指揮體系。海陸與海惠公路雖未長期脫離日軍控制，其沿線鄉鎮與山區之間的聯繫卻被游擊隊反覆插入，使日偽無法同時維持所有據點和所有道路。一九四五年春的連續襲擊還迫使日軍把兵力用於守點、護路和封鎖山區，而不是集中作戰。日偽曾以較大兵力對山區基地實施掃蕩，游擊隊因彈藥、藥品和總部暴露而承受傷亡，但現有記錄不足以逐次核實各戰傷亡總數，不宜寫成精確數字。
impactEn: The Three Districts campaign first altered the deployment of Japanese and collaborationist forces in eastern Guangdong. Repeated attacks on escorted convoys, fuel stores, and isolated posts forced the Japanese to draw infantry, engineers, and transport units from other fronts so that roads could be kept open. Roads could no longer be patrolled safely by small detachments as before. Second, practical working arrangements for joint planning, covering withdrawals, dispersing weapons for safekeeping, and unified logistics developed between the old Nineteenth Route personnel and the Communist guerrillas. The corps gradually changed from a collection of autonomous armed groups into a command structure based on regional columns. Neither the Haifeng-Lufeng nor the Haifeng-Huilai road was permanently removed from Japanese control, but guerrillas repeatedly inserted themselves between its towns and the interior, preventing the enemy from securing every post and every route at the same time. The series of attacks in the spring of 1945 also compelled the Japanese to commit troops to garrison defense, road escort, and mountain blocking rather than concentrating them for a single operation. Japanese and collaborationist forces conducted larger sweeps against the mountain bases, and the guerrillas suffered casualties because of ammunition shortages, medical constraints, and exposure of their headquarters. Surviving records are not sufficient to verify the casualties of every engagement, so no precise total should be asserted.
result: 三區革命的直接成果，是一九四四年十一月至十二月的武裝起義在海豐、陸豐、惠來建立了成片的游擊活動區，並把原十九路軍舊部、原有游擊大隊和地方抗日武裝整合為廣東人民抗日遊擊總隊。它沒有在受降前摧毀日軍在粵東的全部主力，也不能把日軍控制的城鎮和廣汕鐵路說成已被游擊隊永久奪取；實際情況是游擊隊掌握山區和公路側翼，日軍仍控制主要城鎮、交通線與較強據點。到一九四五年八月，總隊正式編為東江縱隊；八月十五日日本宣布投降後，隊伍在海陸惠地區接收部分孤立日軍據點、收集武器並維持前沿警戒，九月三日後全面轉入整編。戰役由此形成兩個清楚階段：起義解決的是武裝聯合與根據地立足，後續游擊總隊和東江縱隊承擔的是持續抗戰與受降。現存資料雖可確認戰役方向、主要裝備、地理路線和組織變化，卻不足以支持精確的總傷亡、逐戰殲敵數或每個據點的日期表，因此最終結果應以可核實的軍事得失為限，而不以未經證實的數字擴大戰果。
resultEn: The direct result of the Three Districts Revolution was that the armed rising of November and December 1944 created a continuous zone of guerrilla activity across Haifeng, Lufeng, and Huilai, while bringing the former Nineteenth Route personnel, existing guerrilla units, and local anti-Japanese forces together under the Guangdong People's Anti-Japanese Guerrilla General Corps. It did not destroy the main Japanese strength in eastern Guangdong before surrender, and the Japanese-held towns and Guangzhou-Shantou Railway cannot be described as permanently captured by the guerrillas. The actual division of control left the guerrillas holding the hills and the flanks of the roads, while the Japanese retained the principal towns, transport lines, and stronger fortified positions. In August 1945 the corps was formally reorganized as the Dongjiang Column. After Japan announced its surrender on 15 August, units in the Hailu-Hui area received the surrender of several isolated Japanese posts, collected weapons, and maintained forward security duties. After 3 September, the organization entered a comprehensive period of reorganization. The campaign therefore had two identifiable phases. The rising solved the problem of uniting armed groups and establishing an inland base; the subsequent Guerrilla General Corps and Dongjiang Column carried out continued resistance against Japan and the reception of its surrender. Surviving material confirms the direction of the campaign, the principal weapons, the geographical routes, and the organizational changes, but it does not support a precise overall casualty total, an exact enemy loss for each engagement, or a day-by-day list of every captured post. The final assessment must consequently rest on verifiable military gains and losses rather than unverified numerical claims.
